newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin backs defence minister over army reforms.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin backs defence minister over army reforms.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin gave his backing on Monday to Defence Minister Igor Rodionov 's efforts to tackle a crisis in Russia's armed forces and carry out radical military reforms.
The presidential press office said Yeltsin and Rodionov, who has issued grave warnings of collapse in the cash-strapped armed forces, had met for 40 minutes in the Kremlin.
It said Yeltsin had dismissed widespread speculation that Rodionov would be fired for airing his views publicly.

"Before the meeting B.N.Yeltsin...resolutely denied widely circulated rumours that the defence minister might be replaced and described them as groundless," the presidential press office said in a statement.
Yeltsin, 66, who spent nearly two weeks in hospital with pneumonia in January and is still recovering from the illness, has gradually resumed meeting top officials in the Kremlin.
But his meeting with Rodionov, who is involved in a bitter struggle with other leaders for supremacy over military reform, had been delayed several times.
"B.N.Yeltsin welcomed the defence minister's efforts to solve the difficult problems facing the armed forces," the statement said.
But the Kremlin leader sent a signal to his aides which was clearly designed to show he is still at the helm.
"The president said there are different points of view on military reform, which is quite normal," the Kremlin statement said. "But it is the head of state who will make the final decision."
During his re-election campaign last year, Yeltsin called for Russia's armed forces to become a fully professional force by the year 2000.
But both Rodionov and his chief rival Yuri Baturin, secretary of Yeltsin's consultative Defence Council, have made clear that Russia cannot meet this deadline.
